lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The CFO's Q2 guide on 2026-06-26 is word for word the guide he gave for Q1 on 2026-04-24 ('net sales slightly lower and adjusted EPS lower on a year over year basis'). Q1 then printed sales -1.1% and adj EPS $0.57 against $0.55 a year earlier, flat, versus a $0.41-0.43 consensus. 'Q1 profit exceeded our internal expectations', and pricing and surcharges put in during Q1 'benefit results through the remainder of the fiscal year'. The Q2 consensus of $0.63 is 36% below last year's $0.98 and only about 10% above Q1's $0.57. Last year Q2 ran 78% above Q1 ($0.98 against about $0.55, from the FY26 total of $3.47 less Q2-Q4). The bar looks set at the bottom of what 'lower' allows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-06-26) beat EPS by about 35% with the guide held: +15.16%. Q2 FY26 (2025-10-09) beat ($0.98 vs $0.86) with the FY guide lowered: -4.44%. Q3 FY26 (2026-01-07) missed with the guide cut: -13.89%. Beats pay only when the guide holds.

findings.finding: Kalwall closed 2026-07-01 ($105m cash plus up to $10m earnout), so it carries two months of Q2 (Jul-Aug). Management sized it at about $85m revenue in the first 12 months at about 15% EBITDA, roughly $14m of revenue and $2m of EBITDA in Q2. Organic 'slightly lower' than $358m (about $350m) plus Kalwall implies about $362-366m. That is above both the $359.5m and the about $351m (-1.9% y/y) consensus figures.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue moved the stock less than EPS and the guide. Q1 FY27 revenue beat ($342.7m vs about $334m) came alongside the EPS beat at +15%. Q2 FY26 revenue beat ($358m vs $334m) still fell 4.4% on the guide.

findings.finding: GroGlass was announced 2026-09-02 and closed 2026-09-18: about EUR62.5m (about $72m) including up to EUR10m earnout, about $30m of first-12-month revenue at about 25% adj EBITDA, funded from cash and the revolver. The company said it 'will discuss additional strategic and financial details during its second quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call', so the FY27 guide will very likely be restated to include it. That adds about $12-15m of FY27 sales at a margin above the group's.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When Kalwall was folded into the guide in June 2026, the sales range rose $50m with EPS unchanged, and the stock rose 15% on the quarter. The acquisition line has no separate reaction history.

findings.finding: Direct peer Tecnoglass reported on 2026-08-06 that the all-in US aluminum price was up about 77% y/y, cut its gross margin to 37.3% from 44.7%, and narrowed FY26 guidance on 'sustained high aluminum costs'. It said commercial pricing passes through slowly: late 2026 for small projects, late 2027 for large ones. Apogee's Architectural Services runs long fixed-price contracts, and its margin was already 5.3% in Q1 against 7.5% in Q4 and 9.7% in Q3. LME stayed at about $3,270/t through August 2026, so the cost pressure persisted through Apogee's Q2 and is the main risk to the guide holding.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Apogee fell 13.89% on 2026-01-07 when it cut the FY26 guide on a tariff and aluminum drag of about $0.30. Aluminum and tariffs are the line that has produced its largest down moves.

The September Midwest premium fell 8.2% to 95c/lb and Oct/Nov contracts fell more than 12%. Apogee's FY26 guide cut blamed tariffs on Canadian aluminum. Offsetting this, a secondary source (2026-09-17) says Section 338 duties stacked onto Canadian aluminum bars, rods and tubes from 2026-09-15; another source says goods already under Section 232 were carved out. Net, a mild easing of the H2 input-cost outlook with real two-way uncertainty.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The tariff line drove the -13.89% January 2026 reaction. The CFO called FY26's $9m tariff impact 'a tailwind now in 27' (April 2026 call).

findings.finding: The 2026 north-west European potato crop is forecast at about 20.7-20.8m t, down 24-25% on 2025's 27.3m t (NEPG). Yields are 7-21% below the five-year average, about half of Belgium's main processing variety fails buyers' size requirements, and free-buy prices sit at EUR 20-27.50/100kg against 2026 contracts struck 15-25% below last year. Stephens (2026-09-28) says the crop 'worsened materially since' the July call. The company guided International EBITDA +40-50% for FY27 before this deterioration. The risk is a trim to the International guide or to the $1.1-1.2B EBITDA range; the offset is the CFO's own 2026-08-14 view that industry-wide cost pressure is 'a stronger base for price increases' and that LW is 'mostly contracted'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: LW trades on the FY guide: -25.9% on 2025-12-19 and -20.1% on 2024-12-19 (guide cuts), +16.3% on 2025-07-23 and +10.0% on 2025-04-03 (baseline). The July 2026 guide moved it +0.8%.

findings.finding: The North American 2026 crop is smaller but of good quality. Idaho planted 298,915 acres, its smallest crop since 2011, and some growers report yields up to 20% below 2025 after six weeks of 90F+ heat; quality is 'solid' but sizes run small, and the Columbia Basin lost only 'the top end' of yield. This follows a 2025 crop so large that LW wrote off excess potatoes in FY26, and 2026 NA contract prices were guided down low-to-mid single digits in April. The net cost effect on FY27 is ambiguous: less waste and lower contract prices against smaller sizing, which hurts fry recovery.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on a crop-only surprise. The 2025-12-19 -25.9% guide cut was attributed partly to industry supply and utilisation (Q3 FY26 commentary: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/frozen-lamb-weston-beats-earnings-165200833.html).

findings.finding: The company itself guided Q1 FY27 adj EBITDA down 'low teens' from $302.2M (about $260-268M) because of carryover old-crop potato cost and edible-oil inflation, with growth ramping after Q1. Consensus EPS of $0.59 (-20% YoY) on $1.65-1.66B sits on that guide. LW has cleared its bar in recent quarters (Q4 FY26 EPS $0.87 against $0.62-0.63; sales and EBITDA above the top of the FY26 guide), so a modest beat on the quarter is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name sells or ignores beats: Q3 FY26 (2026-04-01) beat EPS and revenue and fell 8.9%; Q4 FY26 (2026-07-24) beat by about 40% on EPS and moved +0.8% (baseline; https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/frozen-lamb-weston-beats-earnings-165200833.html).

findings.finding: At the BofA SMID conference on 2026-08-14, three weeks after the guide, the CFO flagged input-cost pressure from the Middle East conflict (oil, polypropylene packaging, soy oil) and freight and packaging costs up 'since February'. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cost-driven guide cuts have produced the name's largest moves (-25.9%, -20.1%), but those were demand and pricing resets, not input-cost items.
